chunks: And ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar narrated from his brother Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليهما السلام, who said:
I asked him about a man who said to his female slave, "I have freed you and made your emancipation your dowry."

He عليه السلام said: "She is freed, and she has the choice: if she wishes, she may marry him, and if she wishes, then no. If she marries him, then he should give her something. But if he said, 'I have married you and made your dowry your emancipation,' then the marriage is valid, and he does not give her anything."

key_terms.أَعْتَقْتُكِ: I have freed you; declaration of emancipation
key_terms.بِالْخِيَارِ: having the choice; possessing the option to accept or refuse
key_terms.تَزَوَّجْتُكِ: I have married you; formula of marriage contract
key_terms.عِتْقَكِ: your emancipation; the act of being set free
key_terms.مَهْرَكِ: your dowry; the bridal gift owed in marriage

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man makes his female slave’s emancipation her dowry in marriage?
ai.summary: This hadith explains a legal distinction in marriage and emancipation. If a man first frees his female slave and then says that her emancipation is her dowry, she remains free and has the choice whether to marry him; if she does marry him, he should give her something. But if he contracts the marriage by saying that her dowry is her emancipation, the marriage is valid and no additional payment is required.
